scopes.name: agent
scopes.description: The `agent` scope controls the default settings applied to agents.

children.name: apiKey
children.description: The API key used to authenticate with the LLM provider. When not specified, the `NXF_AGENT_API_KEY` environment variable is used, then the API provider's own variable (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) when the endpoint it would be sent to belongs to that provider.

children.name: apiProvider
children.description: The provider namespace the API key and base URL are taken from when they come from the environment, one of `anthropic`, `azure`, `gemini`, `google`, `mistral`, `openai`, `openrouter`. When not specified, it is inferred from the host of `baseUrl` when that names a well-known provider, and otherwise from the model id prefix. It does NOT select the wire protocol, which is always the model id prefix.

children.name: baseUrl
children.description: The base URL of the endpoint serving the model, e.g. a local vLLM or Ollama server or a gateway. When not specified, the `NXF_AGENT_BASE_URL` environment variable is used, then the API provider's own variable (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`), then the provider default.

children.name: maxIterations
children.description: The default maximum number of LLM iterations used by an agent that does not declare a `maxIterations` directive (default: `20`).

children.name: maxToolOutputInlineSize
children.description: The maximum size of a structured tool-output file whose contents are passed to the LLM; larger outputs are returned as a path handle (default: `32 KB`).

children.name: model
children.description: The default model (`provider/model`) used by an agent that does not declare a `model` directive.

children.name: requestTimeout
children.description: The amount of time to wait for an LLM chat request to complete before failing (default: `120 sec`).

children.name: rpc
children.description: Settings for the agent RPC broker that a canonical agent task connects back to.

children.name: capabilityTimeout
children.description: How long an agent RPC capability remains valid while its task waits to start, i.e. the maximum queueing delay tolerated between the task script being generated and the agent connecting back to the driver (default: `1 h`).

children.name: port
children.description: The port the driver's agent RPC broker binds to. `0` (the default) picks an ephemeral port; pin it when the driver sits behind a firewall that must be opened in advance.

children.name: remoteHost
children.description: The host name a containerized agent task uses to reach the driver's RPC broker. Falls back to the `NXF_AGENT_RPC_REMOTE_HOST` environment variable, then to inference from the container engine and the executor: the engine's built-in host alias (`host.docker.internal` for Docker, `host.containers.internal` for Podman) when that engine runs on the driver host, `127.0.0.1` when the container shares the driver's network namespace, and otherwise the driver's own address on its default route. Set it explicitly where the driver does not share a network with its tasks: a Kubernetes driver outside the cluster the pods run in, a cloud batch driver on an instance in a different VPC from the compute environment, or a multi-homed submit node whose default route is not the compute fabric. Give a routable driver address or an in-cluster service name.

children.name: tls
children.description: When `true` (the default), the driver's agent RPC broker serves TLS with a certificate generated for the run, whose fingerprint the agent task pins. Set it to `false` only to inspect the stream while debugging: the prompt, inputs, tool arguments and results then cross the network in cleartext, and the task cannot tell the real driver from an impostor.

children.name: runner
children.description: The agent runner extension to use (for example `pi` or `langchain4j`). Required when more than one runner plugin is enabled.

children.name: trace
children.description: When `true`, log a readable trace of each agent's execution - the turns, the model reasoning and the tool invocations - at INFO level; the tool inputs and outputs are logged at DEBUG. Enabled by the `-with-agent-trace` run option (default: `false`).

scopes.name: appleContainer
scopes.description: The `appleContainer` scope controls how [Apple container](https://github.com/apple/container) runtime is used by Nextflow.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Enable Apple container execution (default: `false`).

children.name: engineOptions
children.description: Specify additional options supported by the `container` CLI i.e. `container [OPTIONS] run`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where container images are pulled. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: remove
children.description: Clean up the container after the execution (default: `true`).

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by the `container run` command.

children.name: temp
children.description: Mounts a path of your choice as the `/tmp` directory in the container.

children.name: tty
children.description: Allocates a pseudo-tty (default: `false`).

children.name: writableInputMounts
children.description: When `false`, mount input directories as read-only (default: `true`).

scopes.name: apptainer
scopes.description: The `apptainer` scope controls how [Apptainer](https://apptainer.org) containers are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: autoMounts
children.description: Automatically mount host paths in the executed container (default: `true`). It requires the `user bind control` feature to be enabled in your Apptainer installation.

children.name: cacheDir
children.description: The directory where remote Apptainer images are stored. When using a computing cluster it must be a shared folder accessible to all compute nodes.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Apptainer containers (default: `false`).

children.name: engineOptions
children.description: Specify additional options supported by the Apptainer engine i.e. `apptainer [OPTIONS]`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: libraryDir
children.description: Directory where remote Apptainer images are retrieved. When using a computing cluster it must be a shared folder accessible to all compute nodes.

children.name: noHttps
children.description: Pull the Apptainer image with http protocol (default: `false`).

children.name: ociAutoPull
children.description: When enabled, OCI (and Docker) container images are pulled and converted to the SIF format by the Apptainer run command, instead of Nextflow (default: `false`).

children.name: pullTimeout
children.description: The amount of time the Apptainer pull can last, exceeding which the process is terminated (default: `20 min`).

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where Docker images are pulled. It should be only used to specify a private registry server. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: resourceLimits
children.description: Apply the task `cpus` and `memory` directives as container resource limits using the `--cpus` and `--memory` flags (default: `false`).

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by `apptainer exec`.

scopes.name: aws
scopes.description: The `aws` scope controls the interactions with AWS, including AWS Batch and S3.

children.name: accessKey
children.description: AWS account access key.

children.name: batch
children.description: The `aws` scope controls the interactions with AWS, including AWS Batch and S3.

children.name: cliPath
children.description: The path where the AWS command line tool is installed in the host AMI.

children.name: delayBetweenAttempts
children.description: Delay between download attempts from S3 (default: `10 sec`).

children.name: executionRole
children.description: The AWS Batch [Execution Role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/execution-IAM-role.html) ARN that needs to be used to execute the Batch Job. It is mandatory when using AWS Fargate.

children.name: forceGlacierTransfer
children.description: When `true`, add the `--force-glacier-transfer` flag to AWS CLI S3 download commands (default: `false`).

children.name: jobRole
children.description: The AWS Batch Job Role ARN that needs to be used to execute the Batch Job.

children.name: logsGroup
children.description: The name of the logs group used by Batch Jobs (default: `/aws/batch/job`).

children.name: maxParallelTransfers
children.description: Max parallel upload/download transfer operations *per job* (default: `4`).

children.name: maxSpotAttempts
children.description: Max number of execution attempts of a job interrupted by a EC2 Spot reclaim event (default: `0`)

children.name: maxTransferAttempts
children.description: Max number of downloads attempts from S3 (default: `1`).

children.name: platformType
children.description: The compute platform type used by AWS Batch. Can be either `ec2` or `fargate`. Set to `fargate` to use [AWS Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/fargate.html).

children.name: retryMode
children.description: The [retry mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-retries.html) used to handle rate-limiting by AWS APIs. Can be one of `standard`, `legacy`, `adaptive`, or `built-in` (default: `standard`).

children.name: schedulingPriority
children.description: The scheduling priority for all tasks when using [fair-share scheduling](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/hpc/introducing-fair-share-scheduling-for-aws-batch/) (default: `0`).

children.name: shareIdentifier
children.description: The share identifier for all tasks when using [fair-share scheduling](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/hpc/introducing-fair-share-scheduling-for-aws-batch/).

children.name: terminateUnschedulableJobs
children.description: When `true`, jobs that cannot be scheduled due to lack of resources or misconfiguration are terminated and handled as task failures (default: `false`).

children.name: volumes
children.description: List of container mounts. Mounts can be specified as simple e.g. `/some/path` or canonical format e.g. `/host/path:/mount/path[:ro|rw]`.

children.name: client
children.description: The `aws` scope controls the interactions with AWS, including AWS Batch and S3.

children.name: anonymous
children.description: Allow the access of public S3 buckets without providing AWS credentials (default: `false`). Any service that does not accept unsigned requests will return a service access error.

children.name: connectionTimeout
children.description: The amount of time to wait (in milliseconds) when initially establishing a connection before timing out (default: `10000`).

children.name: endpoint
children.description: The AWS S3 API entry point e.g. `https://s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com`. The endpoint must include the protocol prefix e.g. `https://`.

children.name: maxConcurrency
children.description: The `aws` scope controls the interactions with AWS, including AWS Batch and S3.

children.name: maxConnections
children.description: The maximum number of open HTTP connections used by the S3 client (default: `50`).

children.name: maxDownloadHeapMemory
children.description: The maximum size for the heap memory buffer used by concurrent downloads. It must be at least 10 times the `minimumPartSize` (default:`400 MB`).

children.name: maxErrorRetry
children.description: The maximum number of retry attempts for failed retryable requests (default: `-1`).

children.name: maxNativeMemory
children.description: The `aws` scope controls the interactions with AWS, including AWS Batch and S3.

children.name: minimumPartSize
children.description: The minimum part size used for multipart uploads to S3 (default: `8 MB`).

children.name: multipartThreshold
children.description: The object size threshold used for multipart uploads to S3 (default: same as `aws.cllient.minimumPartSize`).

children.name: proxyHost
children.description: The proxy host to connect through.

children.name: proxyPassword
children.description: The password to use when connecting through a proxy.

children.name: proxyPort
children.description: The port to use when connecting through a proxy.

children.name: proxyScheme
children.description: The protocol scheme to use when connecting through a proxy. Can be `http` or `https` (default: `'http'`).

children.name: proxyUsername
children.description: The user name to use when connecting through a proxy.

children.name: requesterPays
children.description: Use [Requester Pays](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html) for S3 buckets (default: `false`).

children.name: s3Acl
children.description: Specify predefined bucket permissions, also known as [canned ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html#canned-acl). Can be one of `Private`, `PublicRead`, `PublicReadWrite`, `AuthenticatedRead`, `LogDeliveryWrite`, `BucketOwnerRead`, `BucketOwnerFullControl`, or `AwsExecRead`.

children.name: s3PathStyleAccess
children.description: Use the path-based access model to access objects in S3-compatible storage systems (default: `false`).

children.name: socketTimeout
children.description: The amount of time to wait (in milliseconds) for data to be transferred over an established, open connection before the connection is timed out (default: `30000`).

children.name: storageClass
children.description: The S3 storage class applied to stored objects, one of \[`STANDARD`, `STANDARD_IA`, `ONEZONE_IA`, `INTELLIGENT_TIERING`\] (default: `STANDARD`).

children.name: storageEncryption
children.description: The S3 server side encryption to be used when saving objects on S3. Can be `AES256` or `aws:kms` (default: none).

children.name: storageKmsKeyId
children.description: The AWS KMS key Id to be used to encrypt files stored in the target S3 bucket.

children.name: targetThroughputInGbps
children.description: The target network throughput (in Gbps) used for S3 uploads and downloads (default: `10`).

children.name: uploadChunkSize
children.description: The size of a single part in a multipart upload (default: `100 MB`).

children.name: uploadMaxAttempts
children.description: The maximum number of upload attempts after which a multipart upload returns an error (default: `5`).

children.name: uploadMaxThreads
children.description: The maximum number of threads used for multipart upload (default: `10`).

children.name: uploadRetrySleep
children.description: The time to wait after a failed upload attempt to retry the part upload (default: `500ms`).

children.name: uploadStorageClass
children.description: The S3 storage class applied to stored objects. Can be `STANDARD`, `STANDARD_IA`, `ONEZONE_IA`, or `INTELLIGENT_TIERING` (default: `STANDARD`).

children.name: profile
children.description: AWS profile from `~/.aws/credentials`.

children.name: region
children.description: AWS region (e.g. `us-east-1`).

children.name: secretKey
children.description: AWS account secret key.

scopes.name: azure
scopes.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: activeDirectory
children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: servicePrincipalId
children.description: The service principal client ID. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.

children.name: servicePrincipalSecret
children.description: The service principal client secret. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`.

children.name: tenantId
children.description: The Azure tenant ID. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_TENANT_ID`.

children.name: azcopy
children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: blobTier
children.description: The blob [access tier](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/access-tiers-overview) used by `azcopy` to upload files to Azure Blob Storage. Valid options are `None`, `Hot`, or `Cool` (default: `None`).

children.name: blockSize
children.description: The block size (in MB) used by `azcopy` to transfer files between Azure Blob Storage and compute nodes (default: `4`).

children.name: batch
children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: accountKey
children.description: The batch service account key. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_BATCH_ACCOUNT_KEY`.

children.name: accountName
children.description: The batch service account name. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_BATCH_ACCOUNT_NAME`.

children.name: allowPoolCreation
children.description: Enable the automatic creation of batch pools specified in the Nextflow configuration file (default: `false`).

children.name: autoPoolMode
children.description: Enable the automatic creation of batch pools depending on the pipeline resources demand (default: `true`).

children.name: copyToolInstallMode
children.description: The mode in which the `azcopy` tool is installed by Nextflow (default: `'node'`).

children.name: deleteJobsOnCompletion
children.description: Delete all jobs when the workflow completes (default: `false`).

children.name: deletePoolsOnCompletion
children.description: Delete all compute node pools when the workflow completes (default: `false`).

children.name: deleteTasksOnCompletion
children.description: Delete each task when it completes (default: `true`).

children.name: endpoint
children.description: The batch service endpoint e.g. `https://nfbatch1.westeurope.batch.azure.com`.

children.name: jobMaxWallClockTime
children.description: The maximum elapsed time that jobs may run, measured from the time they are created (default: `30d`).

children.name: jobQuotaRetryDelay
children.description: The delay between attempts to create a job when the active job quota has been reached (default: `'2 min'`).

children.name: location
children.description: The name of the batch service region, e.g. `westeurope` or `eastus2`. Not needed when the endpoint is specified.

children.name: maxJobQuotaRetries
children.description: The maximum number of attempts to create a job when the active job quota has been reached (default: `3`). Set to `0` to fail immediately without retrying.

children.name: poolIdentityClientId
children.description: The client ID for an Azure [managed identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview) that is available on all Azure Batch node pools. This identity is used by Fusion to authenticate to Azure storage. If set to `'auto'`, Fusion will use the first available managed identity.

children.name: allowUnverifiedImages
children.description: Allow the use of unverified VM images when resolving the image from the Batch supported-images list (default: `false`). Ignored when `virtualMachineImageId` is set.

children.name: autoScale
children.description: Enable autoscaling feature for the pool identified with `<name>`.

children.name: fileShareRootPath
children.description: The internal root mount point when mounting File Shares. Must be `/mnt/resource/batch/tasks/fsmounts` for CentOS nodes or `/mnt/batch/tasks/fsmounts` for Ubuntu nodes (default: CentOS).

children.name: lowPriority
children.description: Enable the use of low-priority VMs (default: `false`).

children.name: maxVmCount
children.description: The max number of virtual machines when using auto scaling.

children.name: mountOptions
children.description: The mount options for mounting the file shares (default: `-o vers=3.0,dir_mode=0777,file_mode=0777,sec=ntlmssp`).

children.name: offer
children.description: The offer type of the virtual machine type used by the pool identified with `<name>` (default: `centos-container`).

children.name: privileged
children.description: Enable the task to run with elevated access. Ignored if `runAs` is set (default: `false`).

children.name: publisher
children.description: The publisher of virtual machine type used by the pool identified with `<name>` (default: `microsoft-azure-batch`).

children.description: The username under which the task is run. The user must already exist on each node of the pool.

children.name: scaleFormula
children.description: The [scale formula](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/batch/batch-automatic-scaling) for the pool identified with `<name>`.

children.name: scaleInterval
children.description: The interval at which to automatically adjust the Pool size according to the autoscale formula. Must be at least 5 minutes and at most 168 hours (default: `10 mins`).

children.name: schedulePolicy

children.name: sku
children.description: The ID of the Compute Node agent SKU which the pool identified with `<name>` supports (default: `batch.node.ubuntu 24.04`).

children.name: startTask
children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: privileged
children.description: Enable the `startTask` to run with elevated access (default: `false`).

children.name: script
children.description: The `startTask` that is executed as the node joins the Azure Batch node pool.

children.name: virtualMachineImageId
children.description:

(e.g. `/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<group>/providers/Microsoft.Compute/galleries/<gallery>/images/<definition>/versions/<version>`).
When set, `publisher` and `offer` are ignored, and `sku` must be set to the Batch node agent SKU id that matches the image OS (e.g. `batch.node.ubuntu 24.04`).

children.description: The subnet ID of a virtual network in which to create the pool.

children.name: vmCount
children.description: The number of virtual machines provisioned by the pool identified with `<name>`.

children.name: vmType
children.description: The virtual machine type used by the pool identified with `<name>`.

children.name: terminateJobsOnCompletion

children.name: managedIdentity
children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: clientId
children.description: The client ID for an Azure [managed identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview). Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_MANAGED_IDENTITY_USER`.

children.name: system

children.description: The `azure` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Azure, including Azure Batch and Azure Blob Storage.

children.name: server

children.name: retryPolicy

children.name: jitter

children.name: maxAttempts

children.name: maxDelay

children.description: The blob storage account key. Defaults to environment variable `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY`.

children.name: fileShares

children.name: mountOptions

children.description: Specify additional options supported by the Docker engine i.e. `docker [OPTIONS]`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: fixOwnership
children.description: Fix ownership of files created by the Docker container (default: `false`).

children.name: legacy
children.description: Use command line options removed since Docker 1.10.0 (default: `false`).

children.name: mountFlags
children.description: Add the specified flags to the volume mounts e.g. `'ro,Z'`.

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where Docker images are pulled. It should be only used to specify a private registry server. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: registryOverride
children.description: When `true`, forces the override of the registry name in fully qualified container image names with the registry specified by `docker.registry` (default: `false`).

children.name: remove
children.description: Clean up the container after the execution (default: `true`). See the [Docker documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/run/#clean-up---rm) for details.

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by the `docker run` command. See the [Docker documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/run/) for details.

children.name: sudo
children.description: Executes Docker run command as `sudo` (default: `false`).

children.name: temp
children.description: Mounts a path of your choice as the `/tmp` directory in the container. Use the special value `'auto'` to create a temporary directory each time a container is created.

children.name: tty
children.description: Allocates a pseudo-tty (default: `false`).

children.name: writableInputMounts
children.description: When `false`, mount input directories as read-only (default: `true`).

scopes.name: env
scopes.description:
The `env` scope allows you to define environment variables that will be exported into the environment where workflow tasks are executed.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/config/env)

scopes.name: executor
scopes.description: The `executor` scope controls various executor behaviors.

children.name: account
children.description:
*Used only by the SLURM, LSF, PBS and PBS Pro executors.*

The project or organization account that should be charged for running the pipeline jobs.

children.name: cpus
children.description:
*Used only by the local executor and grid executors.*

The maximum number of CPUs that can be requested by submitted tasks. Pending tasks are not submitted until enough CPUs are available, and a task that requests more CPUs than this limit fails. A job array counts the CPUs of all its tasks. Only CPUs requested with the `cpus` directive are counted (not `clusterOptions`), and a task without it counts as 1 CPU. For the local executor, the default is the number of CPUs on the system. For grid executors, there is no limit by default.

children.name: dumpInterval
children.description: Determines how often to log the executor status (default: `5 min`).

children.name: exitReadTimeout
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Determines how long to wait for the `.exitcode` file to be created after the task has completed, before returning an error status (default: `270 sec`).

children.name: jobName
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors and Google Batch.*

Determines the name of jobs submitted to the underlying cluster executor:
```groovy
executor.jobName = { "$task.name - $task.hash" }
```

children.name: killBatchSize
children.description: Determines the number of jobs that can be killed in a single command execution (default: `100`).

children.name: memory
children.description:
*Used only by the local executor and grid executors.*

The maximum amount of memory that can be requested by submitted tasks. Pending tasks are not submitted until enough memory is available, and a task that requests more memory than this limit fails. A job array counts the memory of all its tasks. Only memory requested with the `memory` directive is counted (not `clusterOptions`). For the local executor, the default is the total memory on the system. For grid executors, there is no limit by default.

children.name: name
children.description: The name of the executor to be used (default: `local`).

children.name: onlyJobState
children.description:
*Used only by the SLURM executor.*

When `true`, job status queries use `squeue --only-job-state` without partition (`-p`) or user (`-u`) filters. This is required for SLURM installations where `squeue` only accepts the `--only-job-state` option (default: `false`).

children.name: perCpuMemAllocation
children.description:
*Used only by the SLURM executor.*

When `true`, memory allocations for SLURM jobs are specified as `--mem-per-cpu <task.memory / task.cpus>` instead of `--mem <task.memory>`.

children.name: perJobMemLimit
children.description:
*Used only by the LSF executor.*

Enables the *per-job* memory limit mode for LSF jobs.

children.name: perTaskReserve
children.description:
*Used only by the LSF executor.*

Enables the *per-task* memory reserve mode for LSF jobs.

children.name: pollInterval
children.description: Determines how often to check for process termination. Default varies for each executor.

children.name: queueGlobalStatus
children.description: Determines how job status is retrieved. When `false` only the queue associated with the job execution is queried. When `true` the job status is queried globally i.e. irrespective of the submission queue (default: `false`).

children.name: queueSize
children.description: The number of tasks the executor will handle in a parallel manner. A queue size of zero corresponds to no limit. Default varies for each executor.

children.name: queueStatInterval
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Determines how often to fetch the queue status from the scheduler (default: `1 min`).

children.name: retry
children.description:
The `executor.retry` scope controls the behavior of retrying failed job submissions.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/config/executor)

children.name: delay
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Delay when retrying failed job submissions (default: `500ms`).

children.name: jitter
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Jitter value when retrying failed job submissions (default: `0.25`).

children.name: maxAttempts
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Max attempts when retrying failed job submissions (default: `3`).

children.name: maxDelay
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Max delay when retrying failed job submissions (default: `30s`).

children.name: reason
children.description:
*Used only by grid executors.*

Regex pattern that when verified causes a failed submit operation to be re-tried (default: `Socket timed out`).

children.name: submitRateLimit
children.description: Determines the max rate of job submission per time unit, for example `'10sec'` (10 jobs per second) or `'50/2min'` (50 jobs every 2 minutes) (default: unlimited).

scopes.name: fusion
scopes.description: The `fusion` scope provides advanced configuration for the use of the [Fusion file system](https://docs.seqera.io/fusion).

children.name: cacheSize
children.description: The maximum size of the local cache used by the Fusion client.

children.name: containerConfigUrl
children.description: The URL of the container layer that provides the Fusion client. Supports `http(s)://...` and `file:/...` (absolute, no authority) schemes.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Enable the Fusion file system (default: `false`).

children.name: exportStorageCredentials
children.description: Export the access credentials required by the underlying object storage to the task execution environment (default: `false`).

children.name: logLevel
children.description: The log level of the Fusion client.

children.name: logOutput
children.description: The output location of the Fusion log.

children.name: privileged
children.description: Enable privileged containers for Fusion (default: `true`).

children.name: snapshots
children.description: Enable Fusion snapshotting (preview, default: `false`). This feature allows Fusion to automatically restore a job when it is interrupted by a spot reclamation.

children.name: tags
children.description: The pattern that determines how tags are applied to files created via the Fusion client (default: `[.command.*|.exitcode|.fusion.*](nextflow.io/metadata=true),[*](nextflow.io/temporary=true)`). Set to `false` to disable tags.

scopes.name: google
scopes.description: The `google` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Google Cloud, including Google Cloud Batch and Google Cloud Storage.

children.name: batch
children.description: The `google` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Google Cloud, including Google Cloud Batch and Google Cloud Storage.

children.name: allowedLocations
children.description: The set of [allowed locations](https://cloud.google.com/batch/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.jobs#locationpolicy) for VMs to be provisioned (default: no restriction).

children.name: autoRetryExitCodes
children.description:
The list of exit codes that should be automatically retried by Google Batch when `google.batch.maxSpotAttempts` is greater than 0 (default: `[50001]`).

[Read more](https://cloud.google.com/batch/docs/troubleshooting#reserved-exit-codes)

children.name: bootDiskImage
children.description:
The image URI of the virtual machine boot disk, e.g `batch-debian` (default: none).

[Read more](https://cloud.google.com/batch/docs/vm-os-environment-overview#vm-os-image-options)

children.name: bootDiskSize
children.description: The size of the virtual machine boot disk, e.g `50.GB` (default: none).

children.name: cpuPlatform
children.description: The [minimum CPU Platform](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/specify-min-cpu-platform#specifications), e.g. `'Intel Skylake'` (default: none).

children.name: gcsfuseOptions
children.description: List of custom mount options for `gcsfuse` (default: `['-o rw', '-implicit-dirs']`).

children.name: installOpsAgent
children.description: Enable the installation of the Ops Agent on Google Batch instances for enhanced monitoring and logging (default: `false`).

children.name: logsPath
children.description: The Google Cloud Storage path where job logs should be stored, e.g. `gs://my-logs-bucket/logs`.

children.name: maxSpotAttempts
children.description: Max number of execution attempts of a job interrupted by a Compute Engine Spot reclaim event (default: `0`).

children.name: network
children.description: The URL of an existing network resource to which the VM will be attached.

children.name: networkTags
children.description: The [network tags](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/add-remove-network-tags) to be applied to the instances created by Google Batch jobs (e.g., `['allow-ssh', 'allow-http']`).

children.name: serviceAccountEmail
children.description: The Google service account email to use for the pipeline execution. If not specified, the default Compute Engine service account for the project will be used.

children.name: spot
children.description: Enable the use of spot virtual machines (default: `false`).

children.name: subnetwork
children.description: The URL of an existing subnetwork resource in the network to which the VM will be attached.

children.name: usePrivateAddress
children.description: Do not provision public IP addresses for VMs, such that they only have an internal IP address (default: `false`).

children.name: enableRequesterPaysBuckets
children.description: Use the given Google Cloud project ID as the billing project for storage access (default: `false`). Required when accessing data from [requester pays](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/requester-pays) buckets.

children.name: httpConnectTimeout
children.description: The HTTP connection timeout for Cloud Storage API requests (default: `'60s'`).

children.name: httpReadTimeout
children.description: The HTTP read timeout for Cloud Storage API requests (default: `'60s'`).

children.name: location
children.description: The Google Cloud location where jobs are executed (default: `us-central1`).

children.name: project
children.description: The Google Cloud project ID to use for pipeline execution.

children.name: storage
children.description: The `google` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Google Cloud, including Google Cloud Batch and Google Cloud Storage.

children.name: retryPolicy
children.description: The `google` scope allows you to configure the interactions with Google Cloud, including Google Cloud Batch and Google Cloud Storage.

children.name: maxAttempts
children.description: Max attempts when retrying failed API requests to Cloud Storage (default: `10`).

children.name: maxDelay
children.description: Max delay when retrying failed API requests to Cloud Storage (default: `'90s'`).

children.name: multiplier
children.description: Delay multiplier when retrying failed API requests to Cloud Storage (default: `2.0`).

scopes.name: k8s
scopes.description: The `k8s` scope controls the deployment and execution of workflow applications in a Kubernetes cluster.

children.name: autoMountHostPaths
children.description: Automatically mount host paths into the task pods (default: `false`). Only intended for development purposes when using a single node.

children.name: cleanup
children.description: When `true`, successful pods are automatically deleted (default: `true`).

children.name: client
children.description:
Map of options for the K8s client.

If this option is specified, it will be used instead of `.kube/config`.

children.name: clientRefreshInterval
children.description: The interval after which the Kubernetes client configuration is refreshed (default: `50m`).

children.name: computeResourceType
children.description: Whether to use Kubernetes `Pod` or `Job` resource type to carry out Nextflow tasks (default: `Job`).

children.name: context
children.description: The Kubernetes [configuration context](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/configure-access-multiple-clusters/) to use.

children.name: cpuLimits
children.description: When `true`, set both the pod CPUs `request` and `limit` to the value specified by the `cpus` directive, otherwise set only the `request` (default: `false`).

children.name: debug
children.description: The `k8s` scope controls the deployment and execution of workflow applications in a Kubernetes cluster.

children.name: yaml
children.description: Save the pod spec for each task to `.command.yaml` in the task directory (default: `false`).

children.name: fetchNodeName
children.description: Include the hostname of each task in the execution trace (default: `false`).

children.name: fuseDevicePlugin
children.description: The FUSE device plugin to be used when enabling Fusion in unprivileged mode (default: `['nextflow.io/fuse': 1]`).

children.name: httpConnectTimeout
children.description: The Kubernetes HTTP client request connection timeout e.g. `'60s'`.

children.name: httpReadTimeout
children.description: The Kubernetes HTTP client request connection read timeout e.g. `'60s'`.

children.name: imagePullPolicy
children.description:
The strategy for pulling container images. Can be `IfNotPresent`, `Always`, `Never`.

[Read more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#image-pull-policy)

children.name: launchDir
children.description: The path where the workflow is launched and the user data is stored (default: `<volume-claim-mount-path>/<user-name>`). Must be a path in a shared K8s persistent volume.

children.name: namespace
children.description: The Kubernetes namespace to use (default: `default`).

children.name: pod
children.description: Additional pod configuration options such as environment variables, config maps, secrets, etc. Allows the same settings as the [pod](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#pod) process directive.

children.name: projectDir
children.description: The path where Nextflow projects are downloaded (default: `<volume-claim-mount-path>/projects`). Must be a path in a shared K8s persistent volume.

children.name: retryPolicy
children.description: The `k8s` scope controls the deployment and execution of workflow applications in a Kubernetes cluster.

children.name: delay
children.description: Delay when retrying failed API requests (default: `250ms`).

children.name: jitter
children.description: Jitter value when retrying failed API requests (default: `0.25`).

children.name: maxAttempts
children.description: Max attempts when retrying failed API requests (default: `4`).

children.name: maxDelay
children.description: Max delay when retrying failed API requests (default: `90s`).

children.name: runAsUser
children.description: The user ID to be used to run the containers. Shortcut for the `securityContext` option.

children.name: securityContext
children.description: The [security context](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/) to use for all pods.

children.name: serviceAccount
children.description: The Kubernetes [service account name](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/) to use.

children.name: storageClaimName
children.description: The name of the persistent volume claim where the shared work directory is stored.

children.name: storageMountPath
children.description: The mount path for the persistent volume claim (default: `/workspace`).

children.name: storageSubPath
children.description: The path in the persistent volume to be mounted (default: `/`).

children.name: workDir
children.description: The path of the shared work directory (default: `<user-dir>/work`). Must be a path in a shared K8s persistent volume.

scopes.name: lineage
scopes.description: The `lineage` scope controls the generation of lineage metadata.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Enable generation of lineage metadata (default: `false`).

children.name: store
children.description: The `lineage` scope controls the generation of lineage metadata.

children.name: location
children.description: The location of the lineage metadata store (default: `./.lineage`).

scopes.name: mail
scopes.description: The `mail` scope controls the mail server used to send email notifications.

children.name: debug
children.description: Enable Java Mail logging for debugging purposes (default: `false`).

children.name: from
children.description: Default email sender address.

children.name: smtp
children.description:
The `mail.smtp` scope supports any SMTP configuration property in the [Java Mail API](https://javaee.github.io/javamail/).

[Read more](https://javaee.github.io/javamail/docs/api/com/sun/mail/smtp/package-summary.html#properties)

children.name: host
children.description: Host name of the mail server.

children.name: password
children.description: User password to connect to the mail server.

children.name: port
children.description: Port number of the mail server.

children.name: user
children.description: User name to connect to the mail server.

scopes.name: manifest
scopes.description: The `manifest` scope allows you to define some metadata that is useful when publishing or running your pipeline.

children.name: author
children.description: Project author name (use a comma to separate multiple names).

children.name: contributors
children.description: List of project contributors. Should be a list of maps.

children.name: defaultBranch
children.description: Git repository default branch (default: `master`).

children.name: description
children.description: Free text describing the workflow project.

children.name: diagram
children.description: Project workflow diagram location (Relative path or URL).

children.name: docsUrl
children.description: Project documentation URL.

children.name: doi
children.description: Project related publication DOI identifier.

children.name: gitmodules
children.description:
Controls whether git sub-modules should be cloned with the main repository.

Can be either a boolean value, a list of submodule names, or a comma-separated string of submodule names.

children.name: homePage
children.description: Project home page URL.

children.name: icon
children.description: Project related icon location (Relative path or URL).

children.name: license
children.description: Project license.

children.name: mainScript
children.description: Project main script (default: `main.nf`).

children.name: name
children.description: Project short name.

children.name: nextflowVersion
children.description: Minimum required Nextflow version.

children.name: organization
children.description: Project organization.

children.name: recurseSubmodules
children.description: Pull submodules recursively from the Git repository.

children.name: version
children.description: Project version number.

children.name: configProcessNamesValidation
children.description: When `true`, prints a warning for every `withName:` process selector that doesn't match a process in the pipeline (default: `true`).

children.name: dsl
children.description: Defines the DSL version (`1` or `2`).

children.name: moduleBinaries
children.description: When `true`, enables the use of module-scoped executable scripts via [module resources](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/modules/developing-modules#resources).

children.name: strict
children.description: When `true`, the pipeline is executed in [strict mode](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/feature-flags).

children.name: types
children.description:
When `true`, enables the use of [typed processes](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/process-typed) and [typed workflows](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/workflow-typed).

This feature flag must be enabled in every script that uses typed processes/workflows. Legacy processes/workflows can not be defined in scripts that enable this feature flag.

children.name: recursion
children.description: When `true`, enables the use of [process and workflow recursion](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/workflow#process-and-workflow-recursion).

children.name: delay
children.description: Delay used for retryable operations (default: `350ms`).

children.name: jitter
children.description: Jitter value used for retryable operations (default: `0.25`).

children.name: maxAttempts
children.description: Max attempts used for retryable operations (default: `5`).

children.name: maxDelay
children.description: Max delay used for retryable operations (default: `90s`).

children.name: multiplier
children.description: Multiplier used for the exponential backoff delay of retryable operations (default: `2.0`).

scopes.name: notification
scopes.description: The `notification` scope controls the automatic sending of an email notification on workflow completion.

children.name: attributes
children.description: Map of variables that can be used in the template file.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Send an email notification when the workflow execution completes (default: `false`).

children.name: from
children.description: Sender address for the email notification.

children.name: template
children.description: Path of a template file containing the contents of the email notification.

children.name: to
children.description: Recipient address for the email notification. Multiple addresses can be specified as a comma-separated list.

scopes.name: outputDir
scopes.description: The pipeline output directory. Equivalent to the `-output-dir` option of the `run` command.

scopes.name: params
scopes.description:
The `params` scope allows you to define parameters that will be accessible in the pipeline script.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/config#parameters)

scopes.name: plugins
scopes.description:
The `plugins` scope allows you to include plugins at runtime.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/plugins)

scopes.name: podman
scopes.description: The `podman` scope controls how [Podman](https://podman.io/) containers are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Podman containers (default: `false`).

children.name: engineOptions
children.description: Specify additional options supported by the Podman engine i.e. `podman [OPTIONS]`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: mountFlags
children.description: Add the specified flags to the volume mounts e.g. `'ro,Z'`.

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where container images are pulled. It should be only used to specify a private registry server. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: remove
children.description: Clean-up the container after the execution (default: `true`).

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by the `podman run` command.

children.name: temp
children.description: Mounts a path of your choice as the `/tmp` directory in the container. Use the special value `'auto'` to create a temporary directory each time a container is created.

scopes.name: process
scopes.description:
The `process` scope allows you to specify default directives for processes in your pipeline.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/config#process-configuration)

children.name: accelerator
children.description:
The `accelerator` directive allows you to request hardware accelerators (e.g. GPUs) for the task execution.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#accelerator)

children.name: afterScript
children.description:
The `afterScript` directive allows you to execute a custom (Bash) snippet *after* the task script.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#afterscript)

children.name: arch
children.description:
The `arch` directive allows you to define the CPU architecture to build the software used by the task.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#arch)

children.name: array
children.description:
The `array` directive allows you to submit tasks as *job arrays* for executors that support it.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#array)

children.name: beforeScript
children.description:
The `beforeScript` directive allows you to execute a custom (Bash) snippet *before* the task script.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#beforescript)

children.name: cache
children.description:
The `cache` directive allows you to store the process results to a local cache. When the cache is enabled *and* the pipeline is launched with the `-resume` option, any task executions that are already cached will be reused.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#cache)

children.name: clusterOptions
children.description:
The `clusterOptions` directive allows the usage of any native configuration option accepted by your cluster submit command. You can use it to request non-standard resources or use settings that are specific to your cluster and not supported out of the box by Nextflow.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#clusteroptions)

children.name: conda
children.description:
The `conda` directive allows for the definition of the process dependencies using the [Conda](https://conda.io) package manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#conda)

children.name: container
children.description:
The `container` directive allows you to execute the process script in a container.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#container)

children.name: containerOptions
children.description:
The `containerOptions` directive allows you to specify any container execution option supported by the underlying container engine (ie. Docker, Singularity, etc). This can be useful to provide container settings only for a specific process.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#containeroptions)

children.name: cpus
children.description:
The `cpus` directive allows you to define the number of (logical) CPUs required by each task.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#cpus)

children.name: debug
children.description:
The `debug` directive allows you to print the process standard output to Nextflow's standard output, i.e. the console. By default this directive is disabled.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#debug)

children.name: disk
children.description:
The `disk` directive allows you to define how much local disk storage the process is allowed to use.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#disk)

children.name: errorStrategy
children.description:
The `errorStrategy` directive allows you to define what to do when a task fails.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#errorstrategy)

children.name: executor
children.description:
The `executor` defines the underlying system where tasks are executed.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#executor)

children.name: ext
children.description:
The `ext` is a special directive used for custom settings by some executors.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#ext)

children.name: fair
children.description:
The `fair` directive, when enabled, guarantees that process outputs will be emitted in the order in which they were received.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#fair)

children.name: hints
children.description:
The `hints` directive specifies executor-specific hints as key-value pairs. Keys may be namespaced with an `executor/` prefix to target a specific executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#hints)

children.name: label
children.description:
The `label` directive allows you to annotate a process with a mnemonic identifier of your choice.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#label)

children.name: machineType
children.description:
The `machineType` directive can be used to specify a predefined Google Compute Platform [machine type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-types) when using the [Google Batch](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/google-batch) executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#machinetype)

children.name: maxErrors
children.description:
The `maxErrors` directive allows you to specify the maximum number of times a process can fail when using the `retry` or `ignore` error strategy. By default this directive is disabled.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxerrors)

children.name: maxForks
children.description:
The `maxForks` directive allows you to define the maximum number of tasks (per process) that can be executed in parallel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxforks)

children.name: maxRetries
children.description:
The `maxRetries` directive allows you to define the maximum number of times a task can be retried when using the `retry` error strategy. By default only one retry is allowed.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxretries)

children.name: maxSubmitAwait
children.description:
The `maxSubmitAwait` directives allows you to specify how long a task can remain in the submission queue. If a task remains in the queue beyond this time limit, it will fail.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxsubmitawait)

children.name: memory
children.description:
The `memory` directive allows you to define how much memory is required by each task. Can be a string (e.g. `'8 GB'`) or a memory unit (e.g. `8.GB`).

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#memory)

children.name: module
children.description:
The `module` directive allows you to provide software dependencies to a process using [Environment Modules](http://modules.sourceforge.net/).

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#module)

children.name: penv
children.description:
The `penv` directive allows you to define the parallel environment to be used when submitting a parallel task to the [SGE](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/sge) resource manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#penv)

children.name: pod
children.description:
The `pod` directive allows you to define pod specific settings, such as environment variables, secrets, and config maps, when using the [Kubernetes](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/kubernetes) executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#pod)

children.name: publishDir
children.description:
The `publishDir` directive allows you to publish the process output files to a directory.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#publishdir)

children.name: queue
children.description:
The `queue` directive allows you to specify the queue to which jobs are submitted when using a grid executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#queue)

children.name: resourceLabels
children.description:
The `resourceLabels` directive allows you to specify custom name-value pairs which are applied to the compute resources used for the process execution.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#resourcelabels)

children.name: resourceLimits
children.description:
The `resourceLimits` directive allows you to specify environment-specific limits for task resource requests.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#resourcelimits)

children.name: scratch
children.description:
The `scratch` directive allows you to execute each task in a temporary directory that is local to the compute node.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#scratch)

children.name: secret
children.description:
The `secret` directive allows you to securely provide secrets to a process.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/secrets#process-directive)

children.name: shell
children.description:
The `shell` directive allows you to define a custom shell command for process scripts. By default, script blocks are executed with `/bin/bash -ue`.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#shell)

children.name: spack
children.description:
The `spack` directive allows you to provide software dependencies using the [Spack](https://spack.io) package manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#spack)

children.name: stageInMode
children.description:
The `stageInMode` directive defines how input files are staged into the task work directory.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#stageinmode)

children.name: stageOutMode
children.description:
The `stageOutMode` directive defines how output files are staged out from the scratch directory to the task work directory when using the `scratch` directive.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#stageoutmode)

children.name: storeDir
children.description:
The `storeDir` directive allows you to use an external directory as a *permanent* cache for process outputs.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#storedir)

children.name: tag
children.description:
The `tag` directive allows you to associate each process execution with a custom label, so that it will be easier to identify in the log file or in a report.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#tag)

children.name: time
children.description:
The `time` directive allows you to define how long a task is allowed to run.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#time)

children.name: when
children.description:
When `false`, the process is not executed. Can be a closure to evaluate the condition for each task.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/config#disabling-processes)

scopes.name: profiles
scopes.description:
The `profiles` block allows you to define configuration profiles. A profile is a set of configuration settings that can be applied at runtime with the `-profile` command line option.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/config#config-profiles)

scopes.name: registry
scopes.description:
The `registry` scope provides configuration for the Nextflow module registry.
This includes the registry URL(s) and API key for authentication.

children.name: apiKey
children.description: API key for authenticating with the primary registry

children.name: url
children.description: Registry URL or list of registry URLs in priority order (primary URL first)

scopes.name: report
scopes.description: The `report` scope allows you to configure the workflow [execution report](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reports#execution-report).

children.name: directory
children.description: The directory where the report file should be saved, relative to the workflow output directory.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Create the execution report on workflow completion (default: `false`).

children.name: file
children.description: The path of the created execution report file (default: `'report-<timestamp>.html'`).

children.name: overwrite
children.description: Overwrite any existing report file with the same name (default: `false`).

scopes.name: resume
scopes.description: Enable the use of previously cached task executions. Equivalent to the `-resume` option of the `run` command.

scopes.name: sarus
scopes.description: The `sarus` scope controls how [Sarus](https://sarus.readthedocs.io) containers are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Sarus containers (default: `false`).

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma-separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by the `sarus run` command.

children.name: tty
children.description: Allocates a pseudo-tty (default: `false`).

scopes.name: seqera
scopes.description: The `seqera` scope provides configuration for Seqera services.

children.name: executor
children.description: Configuration for the Seqera compute executor.

children.name: autoLabels
children.description:
DEPRECATED: use `tower.autoLabels` instead. This option is honoured for backward
compatibility and takes precedence over `tower.autoLabels` when specified, including
when set to `false`.

Automatically attach workflow metadata labels (with the `nextflow.io/` and
`seqera.io/platform/` prefixes) to the compute resources. Accepts:
  - `true`: include all available metadata labels
  - `false` (default): disable
  - a list or comma-separated string of short names: e.g.
    `['runName', 'projectName']` or `'runName,projectName'`
Valid names: `projectName`, `userName`, `runName`, `sessionId`, `resume`,
`revision`, `commitId`, `repository`, `manifestName`, `runtimeVersion`,
`workflowId`, `workspaceId`, `computeEnvId`.

children.name: batchFlushInterval
children.description: The interval for batching task submissions (default: `5 sec`).

children.name: computeEnvId
children.description:
The Seqera Platform compute environment ID. When specified, the scheduler resolves
the compute environment directly by this ID instead of listing all workspace CEs.
Used as a fallback when the workflow launch does not include a CE reference.

children.name: endpoint
children.description: The Seqera scheduler service endpoint URL.

children.name: httpClient
children.description: HTTP client settings for requests to the Seqera scheduler service.

children.name: connectTimeout
children.description:
The maximum time to wait for a connection to the Seqera scheduler service to be
established, applied to a single attempt (default: `10 sec`). It bounds only reaching
the service, never waiting for its response — see `requestTimeout` for that. A
timed-out connection proves the request never arrived, so it is retried under
`seqera.executor.retryPolicy` for every request, task submissions included. It must be
greater than zero — unlike `requestTimeout`, `0 sec` is not accepted as "unbounded".

children.name: requestTimeout
children.description:
The maximum time to wait for a response from the Seqera scheduler service, applied to
a single attempt (default: `45 sec`). A timed-out poll or cancel is retried under
`seqera.executor.retryPolicy`, so the worst case for one call is `requestTimeout`
times `retryPolicy.maxAttempts` plus the accumulated delays; a timed-out task
submission is not re-sent, since the scheduler may already be creating the tasks.
Set to `0 sec` to wait indefinitely.

children.name: keyPairName
children.description: The EC2 key pair name for SSH access to instances.

children.name: machineRequirement
children.description: Machine/infrastructure requirements for session tasks.

children.name: capacityMode
children.description:
The ECS capacity provider mode: `managed` (default) or `asg`.
- `managed`: ECS Managed Instances
- `asg`: Auto Scaling Group-backed capacity provider

children.name: diskAllocation
children.description:
The disk allocation strategy: `task` or `node`.
- `task`: Per-task EBS volume created at task launch (default)
- `node`: Per-node instance storage attached at cluster level

children.name: diskEncrypted
children.description:
Enable KMS encryption for the EBS volume.
Default: false.

children.name: diskIops
children.description: The IOPS for io1/io2/gp3 volumes. Required for io1/io2.

children.name: diskMountPath
children.description:
The container path where the disk is mounted (e.g., `/data`).
Default: `/tmp`.

children.name: diskSize
children.description: The disk size for session-level storage (e.g., `100.GB`).

children.name: diskThroughputMiBps
children.description:
The throughput in MiB/s for gp3 volumes (125-1000).
Default: 325 (Fusion recommended).

children.name: diskType
children.description:
The EBS volume type for task scratch disk (e.g., `ebs/gp3`, `ebs/io1`).
Default: `ebs/gp3`.

children.name: machineTypes
children.description:
List of acceptable machine type patterns. Supports exact types (e.g., `t3.small`),
family prefixes (e.g., `m5` matches all m5 sizes), and glob wildcards (e.g., `t*.small`).

children.name: maxSpotAttempts
children.description:
Maximum number of spot retry attempts before falling back to on-demand.
Only used when provisioning is `spot` or `spotFirst`.

children.name: onDemandCostRatio
children.description:
Cost limit on the spot to on-demand fallback. With `spotFirst`, a task falls back to on-demand
only while on-demand costs at most this multiple of the spot price. When not set, the
scheduler's default for the cloud provider applies. Set to `0` to remove the limit, so tasks
always fall back whatever the price. Only used when provisioning is `spotFirst`.

children.name: provisioning
children.description: The instance provisioning mode: `spot`, `ondemand`, or `spotFirst`.

children.name: predictionModel
children.description:
The resource prediction model to use for estimating task resource requirements
based on historical execution metrics. Supported values: `qr/v1`, `qr/v2` (quantile regression).
When not set, no resource estimation is applied.

children.name: provider
children.description:
The compute backend provider type (e.g. `aws`, `local`).
When specified, used together with region to select the matching compute environment.

children.name: providerConfig
children.description:
Backend-specific provider configuration merged into the compute cluster's backend
properties (for cluster isolation). When omitted, the backend falls back to its
environment variable configuration.

children.name: region
children.description: The AWS region for task execution (default: `eu-central-1`).

children.name: retryPolicy
children.description: Configuration for the Seqera compute executor.

children.name: delay
children.description: The initial delay when a failing HTTP request is retried (default: `450ms`).

children.name: jitter
children.description: The jitter factor for randomizing retry delays (default: `0.25`).

children.name: maxAttempts
children.description: The maximum number of retry attempts (default: `10`).

children.name: maxDelay
children.description: The max delay when a failing HTTP request is retried (default: `90s`).

children.name: multiplier
children.description: The multiplier for exponential backoff (default: `2.0`).

children.name: schedulingRequirement
children.description: Scheduling requirements applied to this run by the Seqera scheduler.

children.name: maxCpusPerUser
children.description:
Maximum concurrent vCPUs a single user may consume across all of that user's runs on this
compute environment (default: no limit). A task requesting more `cpus` than this cap fails
instead of being queued.

children.name: shellEnabled
children.description:
Enable on-demand interactive shell access (e.g. SSH) to this run's task containers
(VM and local backends). When `true`, a running task can be reached with
`sched task ssh <task-id>` (or a plain `ssh <task-id>@<scheduler>`), and the
connection survives task completion. Default: `false`.

children.name: strategy
children.description:
Execution strategy within the chosen provider.
Narrows compute-environment selection when a provider offers multiple strategies
(e.g. AWS supports `ecs` and `vm`). When omitted, the provider's canonical default
strategy is used (AWS → `ecs`).

children.name: taskEnvironment
children.description:
Custom environment variables to apply to all tasks submitted by the Seqera executor.
These are merged with the Fusion environment variables, with Fusion variables taking precedence.

scopes.name: shifter
scopes.description: The `shifter` scope controls how [Shifter](https://docs.nersc.gov/programming/shifter/overview/) containers are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Shifter containers (default: `false`).

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma-separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

scopes.name: singularity
scopes.description: The `singularity` scope controls how [Singularity](https://sylabs.io/singularity/) containers are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: autoMounts
children.description: Automatically mount host paths in the executed container (default: `true`). It requires the `user bind control` feature to be enabled in your Singularity installation.

children.name: cacheDir
children.description: The directory where remote Singularity images are stored. When using a compute cluster, it must be a shared folder accessible to all compute nodes.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Singularity containers (default: `false`).

children.name: engineOptions
children.description: Specify additional options supported by the Singularity engine i.e. `singularity [OPTIONS]`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the container environment.

children.name: libraryDir
children.description: Directory where remote Singularity images are retrieved. When using a computing cluster it must be a shared folder accessible to all compute nodes.

children.name: noHttps
children.description: Pull the Singularity image with http protocol (default: `false`).

children.name: ociAutoPull
children.description: When enabled, OCI (and Docker) container images are pull and converted to a SIF image file format implicitly by the Singularity run command, instead of Nextflow (default: `false`).

children.name: ociMode
children.description: Enable OCI-mode, that allows running native OCI compliant container image with Singularity using `crun` or `runc` as low-level runtime (default: `false`).

children.name: pullTimeout
children.description: The amount of time the Singularity pull can last, after which the process is terminated (default: `20 min`).

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where Docker images are pulled. It should be only used to specify a private registry server. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: resourceLimits
children.description: Apply the task `cpus` and `memory` directives as container resource limits using the `--cpus` and `--memory` flags (default: `false`).

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by `singularity exec`.

scopes.name: smolvm
scopes.description: The `smolvm` scope controls how [smolvm](https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm) microVMs are executed by Nextflow.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Enable smolvm execution (default: `false`).

children.name: engineOptions
children.description: Specify additional options supported by the smolvm CLI i.e. `smolvm [OPTIONS] machine run`.

children.name: envWhitelist
children.description: Comma separated list of environment variable names to be included in the VM environment.

children.name: network
children.description: Enable outbound network access in the VM (default: `true`).

children.name: registry
children.description: The registry from where images are pulled. It should NOT include the protocol prefix i.e. `http://`.

children.name: runOptions
children.description: Specify extra command line options supported by the `smolvm machine run` command.

children.name: temp
children.description: Mounts a path of your choice as the `/tmp` directory in the VM.

children.name: tty
children.description: Allocates a pseudo-tty (default: `false`).

children.name: writableInputMounts
children.description: When `false`, mount input directories as read-only (default: `true`).

scopes.name: spack
scopes.description: The `spack` scope controls the creation of a Spack environment by the Spack package manager.

children.name: cacheDir
children.description: The path where Spack environments are stored. It should be accessible from all compute nodes when using a shared file system.

children.name: checksum
children.description: Enable checksum verification of source tarballs (default: `true`).

children.name: createTimeout
children.description: The amount of time to wait for the Spack environment to be created before failing (default: `60 min`).

children.name: enabled
children.description: Execute tasks with Spack environments (default: `false`).

children.name: parallelBuilds
children.description: The maximum number of parallel package builds (default: the number of available CPUs).

scopes.name: timeline
scopes.description: The `timeline` scope controls the execution timeline report generated by Nextflow.

children.name: directory
children.description: The directory where the timeline file should be saved, relative to the workflow output directory.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Create the timeline report on workflow completion file (default: `false`).

scopes.name: tower
scopes.description: The `tower` scope controls the settings for [Seqera Platform](https://seqera.io) (formerly Tower Cloud).

children.name: accessToken
children.description: The unique access token for your Seqera Platform account.

`revision`, `commitId`, `repository`, `manifestName`, `runtimeVersion`,
`workflowId`, `workspaceId`, `computeEnvId`.

The labels declared with the `resourceLabels` process directive take precedence
on key collision.

children.name: computeEnvId
children.description: The Compute Environment ID in Seqera Platform in which to launch the run (default: the primary environment in the workspace).

children.name: enabled

children.name: endpoint

children.name: httpReadTimeout
children.description: The HTTP read timeout for Seqera Platform API requests (default: `'60s'`).

children.name: retryPolicy
children.description: The `tower` scope controls the settings for [Seqera Platform](https://seqera.io) (formerly Tower Cloud).

children.name: delay

children.name: jitter

children.name: maxAttempts

children.name: maxDelay

children.name: workspaceId

children.description: Create the execution trace file on workflow completion (default: `false`).
